gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-cactus-classical-ser: Ruler-straight and unhurried, Bruno Ace lays down one constant line while Cactus Classical Serif brings a gentle swell to its bowls. Drawn-by-rule against softly shaded: that gap is the draw.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-caudex: Spare and drafted, Bruno Ace moves one character at a time, with each glyph looking traced from a single pen tip. Caudex, a text serif, keeps its thin strokes close to its thick ones, so paragraphs go down smoothly.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-chiron-sung-hk: Bruno Ace keeps its counters connected to the outside and every stroke at the same visual weight, giving it a drafted, expressive look. And Chiron Sung HK, a serif with a faint wedge of pen pressure in its curves, makes longer reading feel editorial and settled.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-cinzel: Bruno Ace is drawn with a ruler-straight line that never tilts its round letters, so each glyph looks plotted rather than written. But Cinzel, a serif with a modest gap between stems and hairlines, gives it the strongest foil: classical and loosely spaced against drafted and constant.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-diphylleia: Diphylleia reads like soft metal stamped onto paper, its stems just a little heavier than its hairlines and its openings clear even when tiny. Bruno Ace, with its matching arch and stem, hands a longer page a crisp, drafted start.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-donegal-one: Bruno Ace draws every letter with zero thick and thin contrast. Donegal One, a serif with curves that leave daylight and thins that never turn spindly, adds tempered shading beneath it, so the heading looks drafted and the text looks refined.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-fjord-one: Fjord One has wide-mouthed round letters and a gentle thickening where its bowls curve around, which gives it a refined, editorial tone. A longer passage in this serif would feel steady under Bruno Ace's ruler-drawn headings.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-gentium-book-plus: Traditional in feeling, Gentium Book Plus is a text serif with lighter horizontals and wide letter openings. Bruno Ace is best at a monoweight, expressive statement, while Gentium Book Plus does its best work in the lines that follow.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-gfs-didot: Bruno Ace builds its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, which gives it a drafted, expressive look. GFS Didot, a serif with joins that thin gently and generous gaps in its curves, makes a longer read feel literary and unhurried.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-hahmlet: Bruno Ace traces each letter with a line of constant weight, ruler-drawn and distinctive. Hahmlet, with a mild pressure shadow like worn charcoal, brings a dignified editorial softness that the heading lacks.
